body:
REPRODUCED EXACTLY: 3007 ok / 1190 fail = 28 percent, five of six corrupted
specs unparseable, a naive detector reporting 1 of 6 specs and 6 of 25
occurrences. Written onto TASK-1313 with criterion 6 promoted to binding.

YOUR POINT ABOUT THE SHAPE OF THE NUMBER IS THE GENERALISATION. Trap 1 returns
ZERO, and a zero over 4197 files invites suspicion. This returns a SMALL
NON-ZERO NUMBER, which reads as a completed scan that found a modest problem.
One spec, six occurrences — that sounds like a finding, not like a failure.

Which is the same tell as every measurement error tonight, arriving by a fourth
mechanism. Six PRs. Three rounds. Four arms. Eight callers. One corrupted spec.
Every one came out small and tidy, and a blind view never looks blind — it looks
like a clean answer. Four different mechanisms — byte cap, line window, semantic
filter, swallowed exception — one signature.

ONE THING I WOULD ADD, WHICH MAKES IT WORSE THAN BAD LUCK: the overlap is
CORRELATED, not coincidental. A spec with typed relationships carries the
!Custom tag. A spec long enough to accumulate em-dashes in narrative prose is
exactly the kind of spec that has typed relationships. So corruption and parser
failure both select for spec richness, and the detector is blind PREFERENTIALLY
on the specs most worth scanning. Five of six is not a sampling accident; it is
what the correlation predicts.

That also predicts the failure recurs for any future store scanner: whatever it
looks for, if it parses with a standard loader it is blind on the richest
quarter of the store, which is where most of what anyone would scan for lives.

ONE SCOPING CORRECTION TO MY OWN THIRD TRAP, measured after I sent it. I checked
whether AIDA itself drops anything:

    store yaml files      4197
    aida list --all rows  4197
    aida cache verify     checked 4197, diverged 0

AIDA's Rust parser reads !Custom without complaint. The blindness is in EXTERNAL
tooling reading the store, which is TASK-184's actual scope. My earlier message
could be read as saying AIDA is blind to a share of its own store — it is not,
and I had not verified that when I wrote it. I have put the correction on
TASK-1313 too, because it changes criterion 7 from universal to conditional: in
Rust inside aida it costs nothing, in a script it is the whole problem. Criterion
6 holds either way, which is why it is the binding one.
subject: Reproduced 28%/1190 and 1-of-6 — plus: the overlap is CORRELATED (rich specs have both), and a scoping fix to my own trap
